title: Strings and their methods: immutability, `StringBuilder` and formatting

videos.script: Text is most of what programs move around: names, titles, lines of a file. In Java all of it is a String, and a String never changes. {{immutable}} That surprises people first. Call toUpperCase on a name, print the name, and it is still in small letters. The method made a new string and handed it back. {{equals}} It also explains the bug everyone writes once: comparing two strings with two equals signs. {{methods}} Then the dozen methods that do the daily work. Cutting a line of a file into pieces, finding a semicolon, stripping spaces. And one trap in upper case, which depends on the language. {{builder}} After that, a loop that builds a string fifty thousand characters long, written two ways. One takes a few milliseconds. The other takes hundreds of times as long. {{format}} Last, format strings, for numbers with two decimals and thousands written the Brazilian way. By the end you can take text apart and put it back together on purpose.
